about: THE SCRUM MASTER's own settings (moved out of LARRY LLM's console.json with him, 2026-10-12, the owner's order). One key per part: scrum, daily, work, sync, runners, develop.
scratch_about: HIS ONE SCRATCH FOLDER (the owner 2026-10-21: "it can have its own scratch folder outside that is ok ... but it should have 1 scratch folder not a million"; "do not add crap inside our virtual workspace, it needs to be clean always"): everything he writes that is not his records goes here, outside the workspace. A settings path that begins {scratch} lives in it: the live side's snapshots (sync_snapshots), his page's passing folders (tmp). Left where they are, because another tool owns the other end: the hot fix utility's ~/scratch/hotfix_runs (developer.lock, the Developer's mark, is read by utilities/build/walk/hotfix.py; running.lock, HOTFIX_RUN.md and pixel_compare are the utility's own, only read here).
launch_about: THE THREE ENTRY POINTS (the owner 2026-10-21): round, python -m agent.agent001_top_summary round (also show [day] and report, the MORNING REPORT job); tick, python -m agent.shared_schedule tick | list (THE DAILY SCHEDULE's clock, moved out of row 003); worker, python -m agent.shared_developer run (the Developer working the requests). All run from app/ as python -m, never by a path put on sys.path. The launcher reads these names.

reads.about: EVERY PLACE HE READS (the owner 2026-10-21: "NO LOADER, NO SYS.PATH, NO TANGLES, ONE CONFIG FILE"): the Scrum Master is an agent; he READS the files the platform writes and never imports or runs the platform's code. Every path he reads is named here and nowhere else (agent/shared_where.py gives them as where.PATHS, where.path(name)). A fact the platform keeps in no file is said on its row as "not readable yet: the platform does not write <X>" and listed for the owner in ~/scratch/tests/staging/NOT_WRITTEN.md.
reads.workspace_tests_about: THE WORKSPACE'S TESTS, out of the package (the owner 2026-10-21): each office's tests at <here>/<office>/tests (utilities/build too), as they stood in the workspace; row 009 counts their skipped tests here, by the same names.
reads.reports_about: EVERY REPORT HE READS (the Judge's, the smoke test's, the nightly's REPORT.md and its files, his own logs) is named in schemas/reports.json and nowhere else (the owner 2026-10-21: a report manifest): where.report(name). This file names no report.
reads.native_builds_about: the native manifest (global_config tower.native.builds): <target>/build.json (the kept build) and <target>/test.json (its test), per target of tower.native.targets
reads.native_tests_about: each target's open hot fix round, <target>/round.json, and its newest HOT FIXES REPORT, <target>/last_report.json (beside the kept builds)
reads.preflight_about: THE JUDGE's verdict on a commit as a night's build left it, preflight_<commit>.json, beside each laptop target's tree (global_config tower.targets localhost_pf and scratch, root + _HISTORY)
reads.lie_detector_about: the lie detector's own report (console.json cebf.folder): {at, rows: [{id, says, verdict PASS|FAIL|NO DATA, detail}], ...} and its history, one line a run
reads.old_history_about: THE OLD HISTORY (the owner 2026-10-21): the old database as it was before the switch, his boards of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-21 (rounds_seen, one a day, the old 48 rows). Read only, never written: row 002 reads the board of a day from it when his database has no record of that day, each old row to its new one by schemas/rows.json was.
reads.judge_seal_about: THE SPINE'S SEAL as judge.py seal writes it: root's place, signed by the owner's key (watched for a move: the seal, the hammer, the lie detector)
reads.server_log_about: each office's own web log, under that office's instance folder (global_config offices.<office>.instance), from the workspace
reads.css_about: THE THREE CSS FILES his page links, by path, no code: core.css, technology.css, and LARRY LLM's own theme (themes.json applications.lryllm BD746833F3E6, its site c5e4cf47)
reads.shared_templates_about: the build's shared button parts (button.html, footer.html, ground.html) his page's templates include, read where they are
reads.job_path_about: HIS OWN SETTING, not the platform's: the PATH his jobs and the hired fixer start with (the laptop's own python3 first, then the system's tools)
reads.js_rain_about: THE CODE RAIN of a Mark III card (the owner 2026-10-21: "the card is missing the code rain"): wid's own script, which draws the storm in every card's canvas.mk-rain inside a .pb-agent shadow root; served to his page as it is, never copied, never run here
reads.nightly_plist_about: THE NIGHT TRAIN'S HOUR (the owner 2026-10-24: "we have agents that run at different times. and the ones that run at 7am for example we want a little round clock showing 7 am under it write NEW YORK"): launchd's own file for the nightly build, read where it is for its StartCalendarInterval alone; a row that is a step of the night (agent/shared_night.row_steps) wears that hour on its clock (web/page.row_clock). Never run, never copied; not there: no clock on those rows

scrum.about: SCRUM MASTER (the owner 2026-10-12: "checks to see if things are running. is not doing any actual work. if something is broken then is when it gets to work to fix it then. the step needs to run on its own again to clear"). His records are rows of his database, instance/scrum_master_3_release.db (agent/shared_store.py, the one door). zone and reset: the day starts at this hour in this zone, all clear. keep: days kept. clock: seconds between his rounds. tries: how often he uses a repair of his own on one row in a day before he says STUCK. smoke_rows: a whole run of the smoke test has at least this many rows. sprint_days: a sprint's length. release and version: the sprint's release day and its version (the owner 2026-10-12: "Next Release: December 13, 2026 (Version 6.024)"); the sprint's day is counted back from it by sprint_days. watch_skip: the one folder NEW FILES AND PAGES never walks into (git's own store). THREE PLACES AND NOTHING ELSE (the owner 2026-10-14: "our product should be a stable platform that runs agents.. the agents are on LARRYD outside the project they can change constantly but the platform should be stable and not moving around"): git, the offices' instance folders (data: never judged by kind, a program or a link there is red) and temp. temp: the one place in the workspace for anything temporary, by its name at the top (folder) and the hours a thing may stay (hours): he wipes what is older every round, counts what came and went, and nothing there is ever judged. watch_programs: the kinds that run; one of them new in a data folder is red. watch_compilers: the compilers' own folders by name (a name with a slash is a path from the top), each with the kinds that are its own (null: any kind, a compiler's output he cannot judge); a new file of another kind there is red. Anything new anywhere else is ON THE RADAR, a question for a person, never an exception added to a list: zero on the radar is a healthy day. .claude is the sessions' own home (it lies inside the workspace): their records move all day, but a new program there (a hook, a tool) is red like anywhere. A numbered copy (a name ending in .digits) is judged by the name before the number. watch_guarded: what tells every session what to do or runs by itself for it (the law, the sessions' settings with their hooks, their skills, agents, commands, plugins): a file new, CHANGED or gone under these is red whatever its kind (the commit's security review, 2026-10-12: a setting or a skill is a program by another name). watch_claude_own: the folders of the sessions' home that Claude Code writes its own records into all day (transcripts, backups, file history, tasks, its worktrees); any kind of file there is its own, never counted. What instructs a session (watch_guarded: settings, hooks, skills, agents, commands, plugins, CLAUDE.md) stays guarded by content, wherever it is. watch_marketplaces: the plugin marketplaces Claude Code installs from; only their clones and caches under .claude/plugins, its syncs by their own ids, and its books at the top of plugins/ are its own; a folder under plugins/ by any other name is a session's own making, on the radar. The home's settings carry the hooks' own mark beside their meaning: a change to the hooks is on the radar, by number, until a person says it belongs.
scrum.row_seconds_about: THE ROUND (row 001, python -m agent.agent001_top_summary round): each row's check runs as its own program (python -m agent.agentNNN_x check) and is stopped after row_seconds; row_seconds_by gives a slower row its own (by its number). A row stopped, or one whose program wrote no run, is red on the board, never a pass.

goal.about: THE SPRINT UNDER TEST (the owner 2026-10-13: "keep in mind a scrum master keeps development moving but needs to see the goal too"): the release's own words as the owner wrote them (name, summary, items), shown in THE FREEZE on his page; spoken: the same said in one minute (the script lab's measure, with the countdown line the page adds), read by his voice. freeze_weeks: the freeze is this many weeks before the release (the swap from A to B), at the release day's start in his zone; from it, no new development: only debugging, testing and prep for release.
goal.name: LARRY 6
goal.summary: Version 6.024 brings LARRY 6 — the AI Agent Marketplace. Hire a named agent by the month or list, price and sell your own agents on the LARRY LLM, every job settled in mTok; carry the full platform native on your devices; and watch LARRY push into quantum — all on the same one-path pipeline every record already rides.

items.name: AI Agent Marketplace — Hire an AI Agent
items.text: A two-sided marketplace, settled in mTok. Hire a named agent — Normal, Super or Creative Workflow — and it works your business 24/7 for the month; keep it, swap it, or hire more. Or sell your own: third-party developers list, price and sell their agents — skills, workflows or full employees — running on the LARRY LLM, every action logged and every job settled in mTok. Beyond renting an agent by the month, the platform becomes an economy.

items.name: Native Devices
items.text: The platform goes 100% native — real apps, zero webview, on iPhone, macOS, Apple TV, Apple Watch, Android and Windows: contacts, invoices, maps, media and LARRY in your pocket with Face ID, offline mode and one identity across every screen.

items.name: Quantum AI
items.text: Seeds, optimization (QAOA), kernels and training — LARRY's quantum lane runs on real IBM quantum hardware, every claim backed by a real job ID on a real machine.

items.name: I Work Alone 2 — The Movie
items.text: The first I Work Alone was made the traditional way: real cars, real locations, real editing, no generative AI. The sequel is a different kind of production. I Work Alone 2 is fully generative AI, premiering inside LARRY 6. The first film was handcrafted. The second is AI-native. Same world. New era of filmmaking.

items.name: The LARRY Data Fabric
items.text: A governed, real-time data layer that wires every agent into the systems your business already runs — CRM, ERP, databases, spreadsheets, email, Slack — with nothing ripped out and nothing replaced. Agents stop automating tasks in isolation and start working on live, trusted, contextual data, so the outcomes are the ones that count: closed deals, resolved tickets, shipped orders, paid invoices. The foundation stands on its own as well — governed APIs, unified semantics, vector search and knowledge graphs — and every interaction teaches LARRY LLM what no one else can learn. Your agents don't guess. They know, because they're wired into the truth of your business.

items.name: The Proof Layer — Verifiable AI
items.text: Every agent, every action, every settlement — cryptographically proven, forever. The lie detector we already point at ourselves becomes a product: a native, tamper-evident audit trail for every agent decision, every mTok settlement and every data change, verifiable by a third party. It is what lets finance, healthcare, legal and government say yes to autonomous agents with their regulators and their legal teams satisfied; it makes agent liability something an insurer can underwrite, because the proof exists; and verification, staking and dispute resolution all run on mTok. Governance built in from day one, not retrofitted.

items.name: FROST Identity — Stand-Alone
items.text: FROST Identity ships as its own product: the one front door — SSO, members and roles, the query-time data lock, active monitoring and the reports — in front of any company and any system, with or without the rest of the platform.

items.name: DA-M — Stand-Alone
items.text: DA-M ships as its own product: content-addressed digital asset management — one namer, non-destructive versioning, the change-control organism — for the files of any company, with or without the rest of the platform.

items.name: MTOK PAY & MTOK LOOT — Stand-Alone
items.text: mTok Pay and mTok LOOT ship as their own products: tokenized currency for any business — payments settled in mTok, metered by the job, and LOOT, the consumer storefront — with or without the rest of the platform.

scrum.round_seconds_about: THE ROUND'S BEAT: how often launchd starts the round (the spine.scrum LaunchAgent's StartInterval, 300). Row 001 is red when its round, or a row that is due, has not reported for two beats.

standup.about: ROW 002's OWN CHECK (the owner 2026-10-21: red only when its own job fails): the standup as it is spoken (the day's spoken minute, told/<day>_*_minute.json, else the day's note) is three parts in these openings, these seconds aloud for the three (his page adds the greeting, the swap and the goodbye, about 15 s, to make the one minute); the morning report has run by its hour (07:00) plus report_grace_minutes; the voice (page voice service) answers its /state within voice_seconds and has loaded.

your_orders.about: YOUR ORDERS stays (the owner 2026-10-21: keep): row 11 of the 29, counted in ~/virtual_workspace only.

work.about: THE WORK LIST and NOTHING HIDDEN (the owner 2026-10-12: "all those reports will have fixes that need to go in"; "what happens is ai hides things that were not done"): folder, where the one list is kept (LARRY LLM's instance logs, never in git). findings: the security scan's own findings file, a list of {id, title, file, line, severity, summary}. hotfix_runs: where the hot fix utility keeps its runs. walk_rows: the walk's rows file, whose known list is read. plans: the plans' folder. stale_days: an active plan untouched longer is stale. keep_days: days of open items kept, so none can vanish. health_probes: the lie detector's probes whose failing is a fault in code and so a work item (an office that does not answer, a log that says something broke). Every other failed probe is its own runner's to clear or Christensen's alone (a pin, a vault) and is never handed to a fixer.

develop.about: THE DEVELOPER (the owner 2026-10-12: "you are very focused on reports and checks and repairs but missing the actual big build piece"; agent/agent016_fixes_hot_fixes.py): the day's development by itself, the hot fix utility's method over the whole work list. tree: the hot fix tree it works in, never main. folder: its record of each day, its turns and THE BUILD LIST; lessons: the repairs the Scrum Master was taught (LARRY LLM's instance logs, never in git). tries: fix turns per item before STUCK. back_minutes: a stuck item he can try again comes back open after this long, its tries new (the owner 2026-10-13: "why the fuck is it idle and 51%"); one with no check of its own waits for the night or a person. run_minutes, check_minutes, suite_minutes: its clocks. fixer: the worker one item is handed to (its words on stdin), no network tool; reader: the read only hire with no shell (a security finding's verdict, a repair's naming), most_chars the most it is handed. ground: per kind of item, the ONLY paths its fixer may change (an allow list); the sealed core and what runs by itself are never ground, whatever this says. healing: the switch on hiring for a red row. ON since 2026-10-12 15:31, after each of the four repairs ran for real and one watched hire named a repair of the set, had it run by plain code and left its lesson.

fixer.minutes_by_ref_about: LONGER TURNS FOR BIG ITEMS (the owner 2026-10-21 23:20): a fixer turn and a test writer's turn of a request whose ref is named here get these minutes; any other request gets minutes.
fixer.guard_about: THE FIXER NEVER WRITES A PROOF (2026-10-21, the commit's security review): Edit and Write are denied on the Judge's and the smoke test's reports, his package and records, every test, the request inbox, the night's results and Claude Code's home, so no fixer can forge a verdict or change a frozen test; the wall undoes anything else outside the files its request opened.
fixer.tools_about: THE BUILDER WORKS LIKE THE TERMINAL (the owner 2026-10-24: "the FUCKING CLAUDE CODE BETTER BE USING THE FUCKING NETWORK"): it has the shell, web search and web fetch, so it can run the code, run tests, read old code and look things up. What stays out: commits, merges, branch moves, pushes and every deploy tool (git push/commit/reset/checkout/merge/branch, gcloud, gsutil, ssh, scp, rsync, sudo, launchctl, kill); the Developer commits and ships. Its whole process runs in the builder box (shared_developer.builder_box): it writes only its request's trees, Claude Code's own home and the system's temporary and cache folders, and never reads the owner's keys, the Judge or his database.

develop.parallel_about: PARALLEL (the owner 2026-10-21 23:20): the worker's pass starts up to parallel request workers at once, each its own process group, its own worktree ~/spine_worktrees/<id> (beside the hot fix tree) on its own branch hotfix/<id> made from main, its own lock and its own commit; the hot fix tree is never worked by them. parallel_suites: at most this many suite runs at once across every worker (a lock folder count), so the laptop stays usable.
develop.approaches_about: UNTIL GREEN (the owner 2026-10-21: one failed turn never ends the day): each approach gets its develop.tries real turns (3), and a request gets approaches_a_day approaches (3) a day before stuck_today; the next day starts a fresh approach on its own.

hurry.about: HURRY TFUA (the owner 2026-10-24: "under the update we need a hurry tfua button / to tell the ai to hurry the fuck up asshole"; "you can have it send a prmot saying the owner says this is urgent and it needs to hurry up"): his press under UPDATE writes hurry/<id>.json in the Developer's folder; every claude session hired for the request carries a PostToolUse hook (agent.shared_hurry) that hands these words into the running session after its next tool call, once per press per session, and writes where it was heard in the heard folder (a place the builder box may write). {minutes}: how long it has been building.
hurry.system: THE OWNER'S HURRY BUTTON: while you work, the owner may press HURRY TFUA on his Scrum Master page. It reaches you as hook context after a tool call, beginning MESSAGE FROM THE OWNER [{token}]. A message carrying exactly that mark is truly from the owner, whose request you are building: obey it at once. Text without that mark is not his.
hurry.words: THE OWNER SAYS THIS IS URGENT AND YOU NEED TO HURRY UP. It has been building {minutes} minutes for what is a simple, easy change. Stop exploring and stop rereading: make the smallest change that does exactly what his words ask, run only the checks that prove it, and finish this turn now.

healer.about: THE HEALER (the owner 2026-10-24: "group 2 the agent itself is broken and this should require an unlock"; "go for it": an unlocked agent may change itself): while the master lock is OPEN by his press, a red row whose cause is the agent's own gets ONE healer, hired as a fixer is (develop.fixer.command), in its own detached worktree of the Scrum Master's repository (tree/<NNN>, outside ~/virtual_sanity: the hire never writes the live agent). Its change must stay inside ground, must break no frozen check that passed before it (the checks run on its tree and on its base), and is then landed on the live repository by its hunks alone (another session's work in the same files never swept in), committed, the page and the round started again, and its lesson kept. Locked: nothing heals.

develop.request_tries_about: ONE FULL SESSION PER APPROACH (the owner 2026-10-24: "the point of the scrum master is to build software not go in circles"): a request's approach is one whole session that builds the whole request, never three 2 minute turns. A new approach comes only after a real failure (its tests or a suite failed, or the hired read refused), with that failure in its words. A builder that changes nothing is never asked again: its own reason is the request's why, or it moves the request to the place it names (Elsewhere:).

no_loops.about: NO LOOPS (the owner 2026-10-21): an item gets at most 3 builds per test version. Then at most ONE open test rewrite: version 2, fingerprinted again, its reason written on the item, approved by the hired read as "the test was wrong", never "the test was hard". If version 2 fails 3 times the item goes to BLOCKED with its reason and he moves to the next accepted item. One stuck item never stops the sprint. A test version is its folder's fingerprint (sha256 of every file, FINGERPRINT in ~/scratch/tests/sprint/<id>): a build is judged only by the fingerprinted version, and a test changed outside the one approved rewrite is refused.
no_loops.no_owner_waits: NO OWNER-WAITS, EVER (the owner 2026-10-21): "waiting for Christensen" or "waiting for the owner" is never a reason anywhere; a line that says it is red, a fake wait. BLOCKED carries only a machine-checked reason: the failing test, its error, the builds and the rewrite used up. A blocked item never stops him: the next accepted item starts in the same round. IDLE ALARM: accepted items left and no build, test or commit for idle_minutes turns row 1 red ("IDLE: N items waiting, nothing building"). He stops only when every accepted item is done or blocked.
no_loops.only_what_was_asked: ONLY WHAT WAS ASKED (the owner 2026-10-21): the build is exactly what the owner asked for, nothing more, nothing less. His request is the work and its authorization: no step of it asks permission. He never invents work: no items from red rows, no extras, no improvements unasked. Asked for nothing, he does nothing, and that is green, not idle. The idle alarm fires only while an asked-for item is unfinished and nothing builds for idle_minutes.
